This homework applies the **Bayesian interaction model workflow** from Week 10 to a new substantive question.

**The research question**: *Does the effect of EU structural funds on regional economic growth depend on the quality of regional governance?*

**The theoretical motivation**: A long-standing debate in EU studies argues that cohesion funds only translate into growth when local institutions are strong enough to absorb and deploy them effectively. Where governance is weak (corruption, low administrative capacity), funds may be wasted, captured, or misallocated. We therefore expect the marginal effect of funds on growth to *increase* with governance quality, motivating an interaction term.

**The dataset**: `data/eu_growth.csv` contains 200 synthetic regional observations.

The variables are:

| Variable | Description |
|---|---|
| `region_id` | Unique region identifier (R001–R200) |
| `funds` | EU structural funds received, in % of regional GDP |
| `governance` | Governance quality index, standardized (mean 0, SD 1) |
| `growth` | Annual GDP growth rate, in % — the **outcome variable** |

Work through the sections in order. Your rendered PDF should contain all code, plots, and written answers.

# Pre-Model {#sec-pre}

## Data Exploration {#sec-explore}

Compute numerical summaries and produce exploratory plots for all variables in the dataset.

## DAG {#sec-dag}

Draw a directed acyclic graph (DAG) representing your assumed data-generating process for this research question.

## Estimand {#sec-estimand}

State in plain language the quantity you want to learn from the data, and explain whether this estimand is descriptive or causal.

# Model {#sec-model}

## Formal Model Specification {#sec-model-spec}

Write the full statistical model in mathematical notation. Specify (i) the outcome distribution (likelihood family), (ii) the linear predictor — including the interaction between `funds` and `governance` — and (iii) the posterior in proportional form.

## Prior Specification {#sec-priors}

Choose priors for all model parameters and justify each choice on principled grounds.

## Prior Predictive Check {#sec-prior-check}

Simulate predicted outcomes from the prior distribution alone and assess whether the implied outcomes fall in a plausible range.

## Model Fitting {#sec-fit}

Fit the model using `brms` with four chains and explicit `prior =` arguments.

# Post-Model {#sec-post}

## Convergence Assessment {#sec-convergence}

Check that the sampler converged by examining $\hat{R}$, effective sample size, and traceplots for all parameters.

## Posterior Predictive Check {#sec-ppc}

Assess whether the fitted model reproduces the observed distribution of regional growth.

## Interpretation {#sec-interpretation}

Summarize the posterior distributions of the key parameters and visualize the conditional effect of `funds` on `growth` at low, average, and high levels of `governance` (e.g. at governance = -1, 0, +1).

## Discussion {#sec-discussion}

Write 2–3 sentences reporting the substantive finding in plain, non-technical language. In particular, comment on whether (and how) the marginal effect of EU funds on growth depends on governance quality.
